findings.obligation: Oracle clarity: a name-matched exception line in S1's valid-pairs table, recorded as S1 rework
findings.observation: Line reads '(var r, "AllUnits", false) when r.ToString() == "UnitAdmin" => true,'. It compares the enum by its text because UserRole.UnitAdmin did not exist at RED time; it exists now. Behaviour is correct (tests green, probe red when the production role filter is removed). Non-blocking.
findings.remediation: Replace with '(UserRole.UnitAdmin, "AllUnits", false) => true,' at the next S1 touch.

findings.obligation: Craft decision 2 (an inert AllUnits row disappears from the notice) leaves the Access settings list inconsistent
findings.observation: isSsoGroupRule ends 'mapping.scopeType === "AllUnits";' so a hand-stored TeamAdmin or SystemAdmin row on AllUnits is still listed in Settings > Access as a rule with its role and 'All <Teams> and <Programs>', although the server grants it nothing and the unit notice hides it. A System Admin can remove it. The decision itself is acceptable; non-blocking.
findings.remediation: Optionally mark or hide inert AllUnits rows in the rules table, or accept as is since such rows can only come from hand edits or a newer release.

findings.obligation: my-summary cost: two extra constant queries per non-System-Admin is acceptable, but no S5 test pins the cost
findings.observation: Line reads 'var storedTeamIds = await context.Teams.Select(team => team.Id).ToListAsync(cancellationToken);' plus the Portfolio twin. Query count is independent of unit count by construction (one query each) and S1's 200-Teams count check is a different path. No assertion covers the summary. Non-blocking.
findings.remediation: Optionally add a query-count case for the summary at 2 versus 200 Teams when the cost test is next touched.
